items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: I remember Bunk turning around and beating on the bass drum... I'd like to talk a little about Bunk. I mean, my impression of Bunk as he looked.

ctx.x: That second engagement, if I remember rightly, was the only one when Maude was up there, too. There was something you were telling the other night, the time when Maude was at the table. I forget what the story is now, but you were there once when she was there in New York, too.

Yeah, well, I was telling a couple stories the other night, happening to be at the Stuyvesant when there was conflict in the band, when Bunk was having trouble with a drummer. And I guess I get Bunk actually had trouble with both drummers, Baby and Steel.
I know, even Kaiser Marshall, too.

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: The interviewee (Jerry Blumberg) does not speak about Bunks in the provided context; the mention of Bunks is entirely within the Interviewer's turn, describing an anecdote involving Gene and Bunks.

ctx.x: I don't know anything about it. I think he finished it, and it was supposed to have been pretty good, but I don't know about the publication.

I never did know what happened to him. I know one funny thing that happened one day, he wanted to get Bunks' reaction to Jelly Rolls' Library of Congress records. He'd gotten a few of them that Lomax or somebody had given him tests, which Lomax really wasn't supposed to give out. I gave some later to Charles Smith and I, too, and then Spivak, the head of the department, found out about it and stopped it right in the middle of the series, or after we had about two-thirds. But anyway, one day he brought those up to…
Yeah, well, of course, when I moved up to New York, I think the Stuyvesant engagement was over already. That ended about the 10th or so. Well, this was the second.
